newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea gold prices down on world trend, tax probe.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea gold prices down on world trend, tax probe.

text.p: South Korean domestic gold and silver prices have fallen this week in line with the bearish trend in the world market and domestic demand has been hit by a tax probe into futures trade, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Domestic gold demand was partially cooled by the tax probe into futures traders as most companies are also involved in the physical bullion trade," one dealer said.

The tax authorities in Seoul have issued a statement saying futures traders have been asked to submit documents by April 30. detailing futures trades, cash settlements and official endorsements of overseas payments.
According to data from the Korea Futures Association (KFA), South Korea's precious metal futures trade surged to 158,886 lots in 1996 from 57,389 lots in the previous year.
"It (the probe) is going to take up a lot of our time as we have to prepare documents for over four years from 1993," the dealer added.
All of South Korea's futures transactions are conducted on overseas exchanges, as the country currently has no futures exchange of its own.

Gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell on Wednesday to 10,450 won per gram from 10,550 won a week ago.
The company's silver price fell by nine won a gram to 153 won from 160 won a week earlier.
The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, edged up to 897.70 won against the dollar from 899.70 won a week ago.
The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for companies.

On Monday, the Association of Foreign Trading Agents of Korea (AFTAK) said South Korea's average gold import price rose slightly to $11.47 a gram (CIF) in March from $11.33 in February and the silver import price also rose to $171.54 per kg from $168.94.
